label: Virtue
summary: The plural name of the game concept Virtue, traits that a rite considers virtuous.
details: In a text, `[virtues|E]` shows "Virtues" linked to the Virtue explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts about sins and virtues.

label: Virtue
summary: Another name of the game concept Virtue, the adjective for a trait that a rite considers virtuous.
details: In a text, `[virtuous|E]` shows "Virtuous" linked to the Virtue explanation. Vanilla uses it often, for example in an achievement for having three or more virtuous traits.

label: Vizier
summary: The game concept Vizier: a kind of diarch that clan rulers may choose to appoint to raise their income.
details: In a text, `[vizier|E]` shows "Vizier" linked to the concept's explanation. A vizier has fewer diarch powers but can be very hard to remove. Viziers give their liege extra tax jurisdictions based on their stewardship and raise the aptitude of tax collectors depending on how the scales of power lean. Vanilla uses it in council texts.

label: Vizier extravagance
summary: The game concept Vizier Extravagance: modifiers a vizier buys with their gold while in office, growing ever more lavish.
details: In a text, `[vizier_extravagance|E]` shows "Vizier Extravagance" linked to the concept's explanation. The vizier pampers themselves and the elite of the liege's capital with them. The liege can loot these modifiers with the mulct vizier interaction and turn them into gold. Vanilla uses it in an achievement about looting them.

label: Vizier extravagance
summary: A short name of the game concept Vizier Extravagance, the lavish modifiers a vizier buys with their gold while in office.
details: In a text, `[vizier_extravagance_extravagance|E]` shows just "Extravagance" linked to the Vizier Extravagance explanation. The concept's own description uses this name for the modifiers; no other vanilla text uses it.

label: Vizier extravagance
summary: A short plural name of the game concept Vizier Extravagance, the lavish modifiers a vizier buys with their gold while in office.
details: In a text, `[vizier_extravagance_extravagances|E]` shows "Extravagances" linked to the Vizier Extravagance explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Vizier extravagance
summary: The plural name of the game concept Vizier Extravagance, the lavish modifiers a vizier buys with their gold while in office.
details: In a text, `[vizier_extravagances|E]` shows "Vizier Extravagances" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Vizier succession score
summary: The game concept Vizier Succession Score: the score that decides which candidate becomes the next vizier in a vizierate.
details: In a text, `[vizier_succession_score|E]` shows "Vizier Succession Score" linked to the concept's explanation. The candidate with the highest score gets the post; candidates sometimes offer the ruler gold to replace the current vizier. Only landless and baron tier characters qualify, and good diplomacy and stewardship count in their favour.

label: Vizier
summary: Another name of the game concept Vizier, for the kind of diarchy in which a vizier serves a clan ruler.
details: In a text, `[vizierate|E]` shows "Vizierate" linked to the Vizier explanation. Vanilla uses it as the name of the vizierate diarchy type and in the vizier succession score text.

label: Vizier
summary: The plural name of the game concept Vizier, diarchs that clan rulers may appoint to raise their income.
details: In a text, `[viziers|E]` shows "Viziers" linked to the Vizier explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts and the government line "May appoint viziers".

label: Voter strength
summary: Another name of the game concept Voter Strength: how much weight an elector's vote carries under an elective succession law.
details: In a text, `[vote_strength|E]` shows "Vote Strength" linked to the Voter Strength explanation. Vanilla uses it in coronation event texts about gaining vote strength.

label: Voter strength
summary: The game concept Voter Strength: how much weight an elector's vote carries under an elective succession law.
details: In a text, `[voter_strength|E]` shows "Voter Strength" linked to the concept's explanation. It usually grows with the ruler's rank, but the title's succession law can add other factors. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes `[voting_power|E]`, `[voting_strength|E]` or `[vote_strength|E]`.

label: Voter strength
summary: Another name of the game concept Voter Strength: how much weight an elector's vote carries under an elective succession law.
details: In a text, `[voting_power|E]` shows "Voting Power" linked to the Voter Strength explanation. Vanilla uses it in the descriptions of elective succession laws.

label: Voter strength
summary: Another name of the game concept Voter Strength: how much weight an elector's vote carries under an elective succession law.
details: In a text, `[voting_strength|E]` shows "Voting Strength" linked to the Voter Strength explanation. Vanilla uses it in a succession law description.

label: Wanderer
summary: The game concept Wanderer: a character who belongs to no court and holds no titles.
details: In a text, `[wanderer|E]` shows "Wanderer" linked to the concept's explanation. Wanderers travel the world and stay at courts as guests; they may become mercenary captains, holy order leaders, clergy or city holders. Vanilla uses it, for example, in the interaction that turns a character into a wanderer.

label: Wandering lifestyle
summary: The game concept Wandering Lifestyle: a lifestyle for characters who want to see points of interest or get more out of travelling.
details: In a text, `[wanderer_lifestyle|E]` shows "Wandering Lifestyle" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts about gaining wandering lifestyle experience.

label: Wanderer
summary: The plural name of the game concept Wanderer, characters who belong to no court and hold no titles.
details: In a text, `[wanderers|E]` shows "Wanderers" linked to the Wanderer explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept texts, for example about guests at court.

label: Wanua
summary: The game concept Wanua: a government that shares the weaknesses of the tribal government and also has a smaller domain limit and vassal limit.
details: In a text, `[wanua|E]` shows "Wanua" linked to the concept's explanation. Wanua rulers use gold for buildings and men-at-arms but earn very little gold from buildings; in return they can barter and raid. Vanilla uses it in government and modifier texts, such as a liege being wanua.

label: Wanua
summary: Another name of the game concept Wanua, a government with the weaknesses of the tribal one and a smaller domain and vassal limit.
details: In a text, `[wanua_government|E]` shows "Wanua Government" linked to the Wanua explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Wanua icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Wanua, a government with the weaknesses of the tribal one and a smaller domain and vassal limit.
details: This alias's text is an icon (`@government_type_wanua!`), not a word. Vanilla writes `[wanua_i|E]`, so the icon is linked to the Wanua explanation, usually right before `[wanua|E]`.

label: War
summary: The game concept War: armed conflict between realms, the most direct way to expand a realm.
details: In a text, `[war|E]` shows "War" linked to the concept's explanation. Declaring war needs a justification, the casus belli, and a war can achieve no more than that casus belli allows. Wars are won by beating enemy armies in battle and occupying enemy holdings, which builds up war score. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: War chest
summary: The game concept War Chest: a pool of gold, piety and prestige that rewards the winners of an undirected great holy war.
details: In a text, `[war_chest|E]` shows "War Chest" linked to the concept's explanation. It is shared among the attackers according to how much they took part; part of it is also handed out when the war is declared. Rulers of the attacking faith can donate gold to it before and during the war.

label: War contribution
summary: The game concept War Contribution: how much a ruler helping their allies in a war has done, from the battles they fought and the holdings they occupied.
details: In a text, `[war_contribution|E]` shows "War Contribution" linked to the concept's explanation. After the war, each contributor gets a reward in proportion to their contribution, usually gold, prestige or piety depending on the casus belli. Vanilla uses it in the war results window.

label: War leaders
summary: The singular name of the game concept War Leaders: the main attacker or the main defender of a war.
details: In a text, `[war_leader|E]` shows "War Leader" linked to the War Leaders explanation. Usually these are the character who started the war and the top liege of the holder of the war target, but some casus belli have other war leaders. Vanilla uses it in triggers and interaction texts such as "must be the war leader".

label: War leaders
summary: The game concept War Leaders: the main attacker and the main defender of a war.
details: In a text, `[war_leaders|E]` shows "War Leaders" linked to the concept's explanation. Usually these are the character who started the war and the top liege of the holder of the war target. Vanilla uses it, for example, in the war overview: only the war leaders may make certain offers.

label: War score
summary: The game concept War Score: a measure from -100 to 100 of which side is winning a war.
details: In a text, `[war_score|E]` shows "War Score" linked to the concept's explanation. One side's -25 is the other side's +25; at 100 you can force the other side to accept your peace offer. It is gained, for example, by winning battles and imprisoning the enemy ruler or their heirs.

label: War target
summary: The game concept War Target: the region of the map that a war's casus belli aims at.
details: In a text, `[war_target|E]` shows "War Target" linked to the concept's explanation. If the casus belli has no specific region, the defender's realm capital is the target. The attackers gain more war score by occupying holdings inside it, and after a grace period the defender gains war score for holding on to it. Vanilla uses it in AI army orders.

label: War target
summary: The plural name of the game concept War Target, the regions a war's casus belli aims at.
details: In a text, `[war_targets|E]` shows "War Targets" linked to the War Target explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Ward
summary: The game concept Ward: a child being educated by a guardian.
details: In a text, `[ward|E]` shows "Ward" linked to the concept's explanation. A guardian can take at most two wards. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as "becomes ...'s ward".

label: Ward
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Ward, a child educated by a guardian.
details: In a text, `[ward_possessive|E]` shows "Ward's" linked to the Ward explanation. Vanilla uses it in an interaction tooltip about the guardian travelling to the ward's location.

label: Warden
summary: The game concept Warden: a ruler who has received a hostage from a foreign home court as a pledge of peace or submission.
details: In a text, `[warden|E]` shows "Warden" linked to the concept's explanation. A warden gains prestige over time for each hostage at their court. Vanilla uses it in hostage texts, such as being held hostage by someone as their warden.

label: Warden
summary: The plural name of the game concept Warden, rulers who hold hostages from foreign home courts.
details: In a text, `[wardens|E]` shows "Wardens" linked to the Warden explanation. Vanilla uses it in hostage interaction warnings.

label: Warden
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Warden, a ruler who holds hostages from a foreign home court.
details: In a text, `[wardens_possessive|E]` shows "Warden's" (singular, despite the key's plural) linked to the Warden explanation. Vanilla uses it in hostage interaction texts.

label: Ward
summary: The plural name of the game concept Ward, children educated by a guardian.
details: In a text, `[wards|E]` shows "Wards" linked to the Ward explanation. Vanilla uses it in effect texts about wards gaining extra skills.

label: Ward
summary: The plural possessive form of the game concept Ward, children educated by a guardian.
details: In a text, `[wards_possessive|E]` shows "Wards'" linked to the Ward explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Warlike icon
summary: The icon of the game concept Warlike, the AI personality of a ruler who always wants to be ready for war.
details: This alias's text is an icon (`@warlike_icon!`), not a word, so `[warlike_i]` shows the icon. Vanilla writes it without `|E` in front of the personality's name. Such a ruler saves gold for war before developing their realm, and builds with it after a long peace.

label: War
summary: The plural name of the game concept War, armed conflicts between realms fought under a casus belli.
details: In a text, `[wars|E]` shows "Wars" linked to the War explanation. Vanilla uses it often.

label: Weak hook
summary: The game concept Weak Hook: a common kind of hook (leverage) on a character who owes you a favour or whom you have manipulated.
details: In a text, `[weak_hook|E]` shows "Weak Hook" linked to the concept's explanation. It works in many interactions, such as marriage proposals, but cannot force someone to be your agent in a murder scheme and gives no passive benefit. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as "Gets a weak hook on ...".

label: Weak hook
summary: The plural name of the game concept Weak Hook, common hooks on characters who owe you a favour or whom you have manipulated.
details: In a text, `[weak_hooks|E]` shows "Weak Hooks" linked to the Weak Hook explanation. Vanilla uses it in the hook concept texts, next to strong hooks.

label: Banquet
summary: The game concept Banquet: the phase of a wedding activity in which food and drink are served and the guests enjoy entertainment and mingle.
details: In a text, `[wedding_banquet|E]` shows "Banquet" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it with `|E`.

label: Ceremony
summary: The game concept Ceremony: the phase of a wedding activity in which the spouses exchange vows and are married.
details: In a text, `[wedding_ceremony|E]` shows "Ceremony" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it with `|E`.

label: Wedding night
summary: The game concept Wedding Night: the phase of a wedding activity in which the spouses consummate the marriage while the guests keep celebrating.
details: In a text, `[wedding_night|E]` shows "Wedding Night" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses it with `|E`.

label: White peace
summary: The game concept White Peace: one of the three ways a war can end, when both sides agree the war is no longer worth fighting.
details: In a text, `[white_peace|E]` shows "White Peace" linked to the concept's explanation. The attacker usually still loses some piety or prestige, but far less than in a defeat. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as "The ... ends in a white peace".

label: Victory
summary: Another name of the game concept Victory, the verb for ending a war with the outcome its casus belli allows.
details: In a text, `[win|E]` shows "Win" linked to the Victory explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Victory
summary: Another name of the game concept Victory, the -ing form for winning a war.
details: In a text, `[winning|E]` shows "Winning" linked to the Victory explanation. No vanilla text uses this name.

label: Victory
summary: Another name of the game concept Victory, the form "wins" for a side that wins a war.
details: In a text, `[wins|E]` shows "Wins" linked to the Victory explanation. Vanilla uses it in a concept text: the war target only changes hands if the attacker wins.

label: Winter severity
summary: The game concept Winter Severity: winter drains the supply of armies standing in a barony that has winter, more so the harsher it is.
details: In a text, `[winter|E]` shows "Winter Severity" linked to the concept's explanation. There are three severities, mild, normal and harsh, each a concept of its own. Vanilla uses it in event texts about foraging.

label: Harsh winter
summary: The game concept Harsh Winter: the harshest of the three winter severities.
details: In a text, `[winter_severity_harsh|E]` shows "Harsh Winter" linked to the concept's explanation, which shows the effects of the harsh winter modifier. In vanilla that modifier takes 10 supply, makes armies use 40% more provisions, gives defenders a winter advantage of 5 and adds winter casualties.

label: Mild winter
summary: The game concept Mild Winter: the mildest of the three winter severities.
details: In a text, `[winter_severity_mild|E]` shows "Mild Winter" linked to the concept's explanation, which shows the effects of the mild winter modifier. In vanilla that modifier takes 2 supply and makes armies use 10% more provisions. No vanilla text uses this name with `|E`.

label: Normal winter
summary: The game concept Normal Winter: the middle of the three winter severities.
details: In a text, `[winter_severity_normal|E]` shows "Normal Winter" linked to the concept's explanation, which shows the effects of the normal winter modifier. In vanilla that modifier takes 5 supply and makes armies use 20% more provisions. Vanilla uses it in a trait text about avoiding such locations.

label: Mitigate withering mind
summary: The game concept Mitigate Withering Mind: the ways to slow down the Withering Mind trait, which cannot be stopped from getting worse.
details: In a text, `[withering_mind_mitigation|E]` shows "Mitigate Withering Mind" linked to the concept's explanation. It is slowed by having friends and lovers (the more the better), keeping stress low, and having certain traits such as Family First. No vanilla text uses it with `|E`.

label: Nomadic capital
summary: The game concept Nomadic Capital: the yurt, a moving camp of tents, livestock, people and horses that a nomadic ruler takes along when they migrate.
details: In a text, `[yurt|E]` shows "Nomadic Capital" linked to the concept's explanation. Nomadic rulers grow it with yurt buildings and cannot build regular buildings in holdings; the yurt has a faith and a culture of its own. Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as the yurt converting to another faith.

label: Yurt buildings
summary: The singular name of the game concept Yurt Buildings: the special improvements of a nomadic ruler's yurt.
details: In a text, `[yurt_building|E]` shows "Yurt Building" linked to the Yurt Buildings explanation. In the game's terms they are domicile buildings, many standing for customs or areas of focus rather than real structures, and they can unlock court positions, decisions and interactions. Vanilla uses it in law texts about which yurt buildings can be built.

label: Yurt buildings
summary: The game concept Yurt Buildings: the special improvements of a nomadic ruler's yurt.
details: In a text, `[yurt_buildings|E]` shows "Yurt Buildings" linked to the concept's explanation. They are domicile buildings in the game's terms, and their bonuses include unlocking court positions and nomadic decisions and interactions.

label: Nomadic capital
summary: The plural name of the game concept Nomadic Capital, the moving camps (yurts) of nomadic rulers.
details: In a text, `[yurts|E]` shows "Nomadic Capitals" linked to the Nomadic Capital explanation. Vanilla uses it in a nomadic decision's requirement about the yurt's culture.

label: Unit watch window itself
summary: Gives back the AI unit watch window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it on this type; the same function name on other types appears as an argument inside other calls, which hints at the same role here.

label: Watched units
summary: The list of units the AI unit watch window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list a debug window repeats over (ai_war_coordinator_watch_window.gui). It is a developer window, not part of normal play. What exactly the items are rests on the name.

label: Close unit watch window
summary: Closes the AI unit watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it when something is clicked in the AI war coordinator debug window. Returns nothing.

label: Unit watch window self
summary: Gives back the AI unit watch window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it gives the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type; the same name on other types is used with characters in texts.

label: War coordinator window itself
summary: Gives back the AI war coordinator watch window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it on this type; the same function name on other types appears as an argument inside other calls, which hints at the same role here.

label: War info items
summary: The list of war information entries shown in the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list that the debug window repeats over (ai_war_coordinator_watch_window.gui). It is a developer window.

label: Close war coordinator window
summary: Closes the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it when something is clicked in that debug window. Returns nothing.

label: All attackers active
summary: Whether all attackers are active in the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Going by its name only: it returns yes or no. Vanilla does not use it.

label: All defenders active
summary: Whether all defenders are active in the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Going by its name only: it returns yes or no. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Minimize war coordinator window
summary: Minimizes the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in that debug window. Returns nothing.

label: Rebuild war infos
summary: Rebuilds the war information entries of the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in that debug window. The effect is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

label: Reset shown units
summary: Resets all units shown in the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in that debug window. The exact effect is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

label: War coordinator window self
summary: Gives back the AI war coordinator watch window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it gives the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Toggle all attackers
summary: Switches all attackers on or off in the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in that debug window. That it flips the state of every attacker is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

label: Toggle all defenders
summary: Switches all defenders on or off in the AI war coordinator watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in that debug window. That it flips the state of every defender is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

label: AI host breakdown tooltip
summary: The breakdown of why the AI would host an activity, for one activity entry.
details: Vanilla passes it the entry's own object (SAIActivityInfo.Self) and uses the result as the data of a debug tooltip (window_watch_ai.gui). The meaning rests on its name and that use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The activity information entry the breakdown is for.
fields.values: an AI activity info object, as vanilla passes SAIActivityInfo.Self

label: AI watch window itself
summary: Gives back the AI watch window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it on this type; the same function name on other types appears as an argument inside other calls, which hints at the same role here.

label: Activity option value breakdown
summary: The breakdown of how the AI valued one activity option.
details: Vanilla passes it an option entry (SAIActivityOptionInfo.Self) and uses the result as the data of a debug element (window_watch_ai.gui). The meaning rests on its name and that use.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The activity option entry to break down.
fields.values: an AI activity option info object, as vanilla passes SAIActivityOptionInfo.Self

summary: The breakdown of how the AI valued one activity phase.

fields.name: Arg0

fields.values: an AI activity phase info object, as vanilla passes SAIActivityPhaseInfo.Self

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The activity location entry to break down.
fields.values: an AI activity location info object, as vanilla passes SAIActivityLocationInfo.Self

label: Calculate activity candidates
summary: Makes the AI watch window work out the activity candidates.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the AI debug window. The effect is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

label: Calculate CB candidates

details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the AI debug window. The effect, and that CB means casus belli, are taken from the name. Returns nothing.

label: Calculate scheme target candidates
summary: Makes the AI watch window work out the possible targets for schemes.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the AI debug window. The effect is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

label: Calculate spouse candidates

details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the AI debug window. The effect is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

details: Vanilla runs it from a button click and passes the activity type's own object (SAIActivityInfo.GetType.Self). The effect is taken from its name. Returns nothing.

summary: Whether the marriage tab is the open tab in the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the tab's content and to mark its button as pressed (window_watch_ai.gui).

label: Is scheme tab
summary: Whether the scheme tab is the open tab in the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the tab's content and to mark its button as pressed (window_watch_ai.gui).

label: Is strategy tab
summary: Whether the strategy tab is the open tab in the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the tab's content and to mark its button as pressed (window_watch_ai.gui).

label: AI watch window self
summary: Gives back the AI watch window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name, it gives the window itself. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Open activities tab
summary: Opens the activities tab of the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the tab's button (window_watch_ai.gui). Returns nothing.

label: Open CB tab
summary: Opens the casus belli (CB) tab of the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the tab's button (window_watch_ai.gui). Returns nothing.

label: Open economy tab
summary: Opens the economy tab of the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the tab's button (window_watch_ai.gui). Returns nothing.

label: Open marriage tab
summary: Opens the marriage tab of the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the tab's button (window_watch_ai.gui). Returns nothing.

label: Open scheme tab
summary: Opens the scheme tab of the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the tab's button (window_watch_ai.gui). Returns nothing.

label: Open strategy tab
summary: Opens the strategy tab of the AI watch window.
details: Vanilla runs it from the tab's button (window_watch_ai.gui). Returns nothing.

label: Toggle pause on change
summary: Switches the AI watch window's "pause when something changes" option on or off.
details: Vanilla runs it from a checkbox click (window_watch_ai.gui); the checkbox state comes from the matching WillPauseOnChange. What it controls is taken from the two names. Returns nothing.

label: Pauses on change
summary: Whether the AI watch window will pause the game when something changes.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a checkbox (window_watch_ai.gui). The meaning rests on the name.

label: Accolade itself
summary: Gives back the accolade itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it on this type; the same function name on other types appears as an argument inside other calls, which hints at the same role here.

label: Active effects for a type
summary: Text listing the effects the accolade currently gives for one accolade type.
details: Vanilla uses it in a tooltip headed "Active ... Effects" for an obtained accolade type (accolades_l_english.yml). It returns text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The accolade type whose effects are listed.

label: Active rank effects
summary: Text listing the effects of the accolade's current rank.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a tooltip (gui/shared/cooltip.gui). It returns text. That these are the current rank's effects rests on the name.

label: Next rank effects for a type
summary: Text listing the effects the accolade would give at its next rank for one accolade type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the "Next rank ... Effects" text of the upgrade tooltip (accolades_l_english.yml). It returns text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The accolade type whose next-rank effects are listed.

label: Can be successor
summary: Whether a given character can be the accolade's successor.
details: Going by its name and the successor functions next to it, it returns yes or no for the character passed in. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Accolade custom text
summary: Probably a custom localization text for the accolade, chosen by its name.
details: Vanilla does not use it on accolades. The same-named function on other types, such as characters, is how texts call a custom localization entry (for example Character.Custom('...')), so this is probably the same for accolades. It returns text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom localization entry to use.
fields.values: a custom localization key in quotes

label: Destroy accolade
summary: Destroys the accolade.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the accolade window (window_accolade.gui). Returns nothing.

label: Acclaimed knight
summary: The accolade's acclaimed knight.
details: Vanilla chains it with character functions to show the knight's name, in texts and in the accolade window. It is shown as "Acclaimed knight" in the game's own text.

label: Level-up points available
summary: The number of level-up points the accolade has available.
details: Vanilla shows it as a value in a text and compares it with zero in the accolade window to decide what to show. It is a whole number.

label: Available accolade types
summary: The list of accolade types that can still be chosen for the accolade.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Badge color
summary: The color of the accolade's badge.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Rank bar icon
summary: The icon for one rank step on the accolade window's rank bar.
details: Vanilla passes the position of the bar item and uses the result as a texture (window_accolade.gui).

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The position of one item on the rank bar.
fields.values: a whole number; vanilla passes the bar item's own index

label: Rank bar tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for one rank step on the accolade window's rank bar.
details: Vanilla passes the position of the bar item (window_accolade.gui). It returns text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The position of one item on the rank bar.
fields.values: a whole number; vanilla passes the bar item's own index

label: Current rank icon
summary: The icon of the accolade's current rank.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the accolade window (window_accolade.gui).

label: Current rank number
summary: The number of the accolade's current rank.
details: Vanilla shows it in texts next to the glory value and compares it with 5 in the accolade window. It is a whole number.

label: Accolade glory
summary: The amount of glory the accolade has.
details: Vanilla shows it in glory texts and tooltips, formatted without decimals. It returns a fixed-point number.

label: Glory at last unlock
summary: The glory needed for the accolade's last rank unlock.
details: Going by its name and the matching GetGloryForNextUnlock. Vanilla does not use it. It returns a fixed-point number.

label: Glory for next unlock
summary: The glory the accolade needs to reach its next rank.
details: Vanilla shows it as the "Next rank" line of the glory tooltip (accolades_l_english.yml). It returns a fixed-point number.

label: Glory tooltip
summary: The tooltip text about the accolade's glory.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it. It returns text.

label: Accolade history
summary: The list of history entries of the accolade.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list the accolade window repeats over (window_accolade.gui).

label: Accolade ID
summary: The accolade's ID number.
details: Vanilla passes it to the call that opens the accolade view (window_knights.gui). It is a whole number.

label: Accolade name
summary: The accolade's name, as text with a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts such as "... gained ... glory". It returns text; the sibling GetNameNoTooltip suggests this one carries a tooltip.

label: Accolade name, plain
summary: The accolade's name as plain text, without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts about assigning an acclaimed knight (accolades_l_english.yml). It returns text.

label: Obtained accolade types
summary: The list of accolade types the accolade has obtained.
details: Vanilla uses it as a list in the accolade window and in a tooltip (window_accolade.gui, cooltip.gui).

label: Accolade owner
summary: The character who owns the accolade.
details: Vanilla chains it with GetCulture to pick the accolade window's illustration (window_accolade.gui), so it gives something with a culture, most likely a character.

label: Set acclaimed knight tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for assigning a character as the acclaimed knight.
details: Going by its name; the argument is probably the character. Vanilla does not use it. It returns text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would be assigned, going by the name.

label: Set successor tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for setting a character as the accolade's successor.
details: Going by its name; the argument is probably the character. Vanilla does not use it. It returns text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would become successor, going by the name.

label: Accolade successor
summary: The accolade's successor.
details: Vanilla shows the successor's name ("Successor: ...") and checks it with IsValid before showing the line (accolades_l_english.yml, cooltip.gui). That the successor is a character rests on the use of GetUIName.

label: Successor requirements
summary: Text describing what a successor must meet.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it. It returns text.

label: Meets accolade requirements
summary: Whether a given character meets the requirements for the accolade.
details: Going by its name; the argument is probably the character. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character to check, going by the name.

label: Has active effects
summary: Whether the accolade currently has active effects.
details: Vanilla uses it to decide whether to show the effects part in the accolade window and in a tooltip (window_accolade.gui, cooltip.gui).

label: Has potential successor
summary: Whether the accolade has a possible successor.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Meets successor requirements
summary: Whether a given character meets the requirements to be the successor.
details: Going by its name; the argument is probably the character. Vanilla does not use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character to check, going by the name.

label: Accolade exists
summary: Whether the accolade is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it as a visibility check in a tooltip (gui/shared/cooltip.gui). The same name is common on other types.

label: Add accolade type command
summary: Builds the command that adds an accolade type to the accolade.
details: Vanilla wraps it in a validity check to enable a button, passing the type chosen in the selection view (window_accolade_attribute_selection.gui). It only builds the command; running it is a separate step.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an accolade type, as vanilla passes the selected type

label: Accolade as script scope
summary: Probably turns the accolade into something script values can be asked of.
details: Vanilla has no use of it on this type. On other types, texts call MakeScope and then ask script values from the result, so it is probably the same here.
